chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Husayn al-Sahhaf: 'O Husayn! Allah does not manifest the bounties upon a servant until he manifests the provision/cost of the people upon him. So whoever is patient for them and stands by their affairs, Allah will increase His bounties upon him in their eyes; and whoever is not patient for them and does not stand by their affairs, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will remove that bounty from him.'

key_terms.قَامَ بِشَأْنِهِمْ: Stood by their affairs/Managed their needs

ai.seo_question: How does providing for others affect one's own divine blessings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the reciprocal relationship between divine favor (*ni'am*) and social responsibility, emphasizing that God's visible blessings are contingent upon the bearer's capacity to shoulder the burdens (*ma'unah*) of the community. This teaching underscores a key Shia ethical principle: spiritual and material prosperity are not static endowments but dynamic trusts that expand through patience and active service to others, while neglect results in their diminishment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> to Husayn Al-Sahhaf: ‘O Husayn! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Extend the Bounties upon a servant until he passes on the provisions upon the people. So the one who is patient to them and stands with their concerns, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Increase in His<sup>azwj</sup> Bounties upon him with them, and the one who is not patient to them and does not stand with their concerns, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Stops from him that Bounty’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to Husayn al-Sahhaf, ‘O Husayn, whenever Allah grants abundant bounties to a person, his spending for people also increases. If one remains patient for spending on people, Allah increases the bounties for him before people. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, removes the bounties from one who does not remain patient for spending on people’s affairs.’”
